# 畫繼

**ID:** KR3h0030
**Custom ID:** ZB3h0030

**Extent:** 10 卷
**Base edition:** WYG

## Authors / Editors
- 鄧椿 (宋朝) 撰 fl. 1127 - 1167

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

Dèng Chūn's continuation, in ten *juàn*, of Zhāng Yànyuǎn's [KR3h0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3h/KR3h0009) *Lìdài mínghuà jì* (which ran from antiquity to *Huìchāng* 1, 841) and Guō Ruòxū's [KR3h0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3h/KR3h0017) *Túhuà jiànwén zhì* (from *Huìchāng* through *Xīnínɡ* 7, 1074): hence "*Jì*" — "continuation." It covers the ninety-four years from *Xīnínɡ* 7 (1074) to *Qiándào* 3 (1167), recording 219 painters. The work is divided into three parts: (a) *juàn* 1–5 by social category (*Shèngyì* 聖藝 imperial painting; *Hóuwáng guìqì* 侯王貴戚 princes; *Xuānmiǎn cáixián* 軒冕材賢 high officials; *Yánxué shàngshì* 巖穴上士 recluses; *Jìnshēn wéibù* 搢紳韋布 minor officials and commoners; *Dàorén nàzǐ* 道人衲子 Daoists and monks; *Shìzhòu fùnǚ jí huànzhě* 世胄婦女及宦者 hereditary clansmen, women and eunuchs); (b) *juàn* 6–7 by genre (immortals and Daoists/Buddhists; figures and portraiture; landscape and rocks; flower-bamboo-bird; beasts-insects-fish; architecture-boats-carriages; vegetables-fruits-medicinal herbs; minor scenes and mixed paintings); (c) *juàn* 8 *Míngxīn juépǐn* 銘心絕品 — Dèng's record of works he had seen and could not forget; *juàn* 9–10 *Záshuō* 雜說 in two parts (*Lùnyuǎn* 論遠 on the ancients, *Lùnjìn* 論近 on contemporaries). The book is the principal Southern Sòng source for late-Northern-Sòng and early-Southern-Sòng painting, especially for the Huīzōng academy and the great pictorial collections of Zhèng Yún 鄭雲, Lǐ Cángyī 李藏一, Liú Yìshàn 劉益善 and Lǚ Líng 呂凌.

**Abstract**

Dèng Chūn (a man of Shuāngliú 雙流 in Shǔ, *fl.* 1127–1167), the grandson of Huīzōng's *Zhī Shūmìyuàn shì* Dèng Xúnwǔ 鄧洵武, was uniquely positioned to record both the late-Huī-zōng academy and the early Southern Sòng painters: his family had access to the Huīzōng inner circle and inherited its painting collection, and he himself lived to see the *Qiándào* (1165–1173) consolidation of the *Lín'ān* court's painting establishment. The Sìkù editors particularly praise his methodological balance: he neither idealises the Huīzōng academy's *géwù shǒufǎ* (investigative literalism) nor over-elevates the unrestrained Five-Dynasties-Sòng brushwork of Shí Kè. His third major innovation, the *Míngxīn juépǐn* chapter, opens a new genre — the *personal sighting register* of unforgettable works — that connoisseurs from Yuán *Shānhúwǎng* through Míng *Qīnghé shūhuà fǎng* take up as a model. Internal *post quem* 1167, the date of *Qiándào* 3.
